newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW - Volvo to keep up product development.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Volvo to keep up product development.

text.p: Swedish carmaker Volvo plans to invest between five and six percent of sales revenue in product development but will not allow costs to affect profitability, Volvo CEO Soren Gyll told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday.

"We have a plan to to invest the equivalent of five to six percent of our sales value in product development. This means that the investments will increase as sales do. But there is no choice here, to further our product development is a must in the competitive situation we are in," Gyll said.
"Big investments in product development also tend to add on other types of costs. That is what has happened in Volvo, but now we have to strive to become more cost-efficient," Gyll said.
Cutting costs is on the Volvo priority list and one of the aims of the so called "Agenda 96" the company.
Gyll did not want to expand on his statement a week ago, that a board meeting in October or November will take important decisions about enhancing Volvo's profitability.

"In this process we will look at our structures and also our purchases. Every year Volvo makes billions of crowns worth of purchases not directly related to specific divisions. These purchases will have to be made more efficiently and we will use all the benefits of our name in the process," Gyll said.
